cues.zh: 一颗标准子弹，

cues.zh: 所以

cues.zh: 它流经下水道，进入污水处理厂，第一步是去除所有固体物质。我们把它取出来，干燥处理，就成了很细的粉末。

cues.zh: 故事里之类的？你知道吗，我在这里待了很久，所以我不会从那个角度去想，但我得说，是的。对我来说，科幻元素就像是：真有人在想那个？真有人在收集那个？

cues.en: It seems so fictional.

cues.zh: 这里有苹果叶、桃叶、牡蛎组织、锌金属棒、氮气中的二氧化碳。

cues.en: In these vats of liquid nitrogen, there are samples of marine animals.
cues.zh: 这些液氮罐里，有海洋动物的样本。

cues.en: Muscle samples, dolphin samples, whale samples, birds as well, bird tissue,
cues.zh: 肌肉样本、海豚样本、鲸鱼样本，还有鸟类，鸟类组织，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: and some human tissue as well.
cues.zh: 还有一些人体组织。

cues.en: But perhaps the weirdest thing they sell is something really mundane,
cues.zh: 但也许他们卖的最奇怪的东西其实非常平常，

cues.en: peanut butter.
cues.zh: 花生酱。

cues.en: It looks like a peanut butter. It is peanut butter. It's creamy. It's probably the most expensive jar of peanut butter in the whole world.
cues.zh: 看起来像花生酱。它就是花生酱。口感很细腻。这大概是全世界最贵的一罐花生酱。

cues.en: We essentially pay for a company to make generic peanut butter. We might have 2,000 jars of generic peanut butter, what we do is we then go through and measure the fats in these jars and figure out how much of various compounds are in there, and we actually then slap on a label and provide a certificate at the end. Have you ever eaten some of this peanut butter? All of these things are not for human consumption because I don't know if I could actually tell you how old it is,
cues.zh: 我们基本上是付钱让一家公司生产普通花生酱。我们可能有2000罐普通花生酱，接下来会逐一检测这些罐子里的脂肪，弄清其中各种化合物的含量，然后贴上标签，最后提供一份证书。你吃过这种花生酱吗？这些东西都不是给人吃的，因为我都不确定能不能说清它有多久了，

cues.en: but it's old enough that you probably don't wanna eat it. How much does it cost? These are not sold at commercial grade prices. So this jar of peanut butter is not $3.99.
cues.zh: 但它已经旧到你可能不想吃了。它多少钱？这些可不是按商业级价格卖的。所以这罐花生酱不是3.99美元。

cues.en: This jar, I believe, is around a thousand dollars. This is not something that would be viable for you to make your peanut butter and jelly sandwich with.
cues.zh: 这个罐子，我估计大概要一千美元。拿它来做花生酱果酱三明治可不现实。

cues.en: An ordinary jar of peanut butter costs less than $5.
cues.zh: 一罐普通的花生酱不到5美元。

cues.en: And on the label, you can see the ingredients and the amounts of different nutrients like protein, fats, sugar, and sodium.
cues.zh: 标签上可以看到配料，以及蛋白质、脂肪、糖和钠等不同营养成分的含量。

cues.en: Those values have been measured by the manufacturer using different machines and analytical techniques.
cues.zh: 这些数值是制造商用不同的仪器和分析技术测量出来的。

cues.en: But how do you know those results are accurate?
cues.zh: 但你怎么知道这些结果是准确的？

cues.en: Well, this is where the government's standard jar of peanut butter comes in. It is mixed up so carefully and thoroughly that each jar contains exactly the same substance. We take great pains at homogenizing
cues.zh: 嗯，这就轮到政府的标准花生酱罐登场了。它被搅拌得极其仔细、充分，所以每罐都含有完全相同的物质。我们煞费苦心地做均质化处理

cues.en: these things to make sure it's consistent.
cues.zh: 这些物质，以确保它保持一致。

cues.en: Then scientists at the National Institute of Standards and Technology, NIST,
cues.zh: 然后，美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的科学家们，

cues.en: take years to painstakingly
cues.zh: 花费数年时间，煞费苦心地

cues.en: identify the quantities of all the different compounds in the peanut butter with specified uncertainties.
cues.zh: 鉴定花生酱中所有不同化合物的含量，并给出规定的不确定度。

cues.en: This peanut butter is then known as a standard reference material or SRM.
cues.zh: 这种花生酱随后被称为标准参考物质，即 SRM。

cues.en: They sell these perfectly characterized SRM samples of peanut butter to researchers and manufacturers
cues.zh: 他们把这些特性经过精确测定的 SRM 花生酱样品卖给研究人员和制造商，

cues.en: so they can calibrate their equipment.
cues.zh: 以便他们校准自己的设备。

cues.en: Essentially, the buyer knows that their equipment is working properly if when they run the standard peanut butter, they get the values NIST supplies on the certificate.
cues.zh: 本质上，买家检测这种标准花生酱时，如果得到的是 NIST 在证书上提供的数值，就知道自己的设备运行正常。

cues.en: We've spent a lot of time to make sure that we're confident and, you know, we can spend years studying the amount of fat in here and try to figure out exactly what those numbers are. So what you're paying for is not really the peanut butter.
cues.zh: 我们花了很多时间确保自己有把握，你知道，我们可能花好几年研究这里面的脂肪含量，设法弄清那些数字到底是多少。所以你花钱买的其实不是花生酱。

cues.en: It's the knowledge of exactly what is in the peanut butter. And so this is what really drives the cost
cues.zh: 关键在于确切知道花生酱里有什么。因此，真正决定成本的，

cues.en: of a standard reference material,
cues.zh: 对标准参考物质而言，

cues.en: is our ability to assert the truth. We produce what I call truth in a bottle.
cues.zh: 是我们断言真相的能力。我们生产的是我所说的“瓶装真相”。

cues.en: You might think, why does it matter that the label on my peanut butter is accurate? But it is way more than the things on the label that NIST measures.
cues.zh: 你可能会想，我花生酱上的标签准不准，有什么关系？但 NIST 测量的远不止标签上的那些东西。

cues.en: Peanut butter actually contains
cues.zh: 花生酱实际上含有

cues.en: naturally occurring aflatoxins.
cues.zh: 天然存在的黄曲霉毒素。

cues.en: They're a carcinogen which can cause liver cancer,
cues.zh: 它们是致癌物，会导致肝癌，

cues.en: and they're produced by fungi on the peanuts. So if your peanut butter is made from a bad batch of peanuts, you want the factory to be able to accurately detect elevated levels of aflatoxins.
cues.zh: 它们由花生上的真菌产生。所以，如果你的花生酱是用一批坏花生做的，你会希望工厂能准确检测出黄曲霉毒素是否超标。

cues.en: And they're able to do that because the standard peanut butter contains a known level of aflatoxin that can be used to calibrate their equipment. Would the FDA,
cues.zh: 而他们能做到这一点，是因为标准花生酱含有已知水平的黄曲霉毒素，可用于校准他们的设备。FDA 会不会，

cues.en: like,
cues.zh: 比如，

cues.en: sample
cues.zh: 抽样

cues.en: peanut butters and look for aflatoxin? A lot of times you actually have commercial laboratories that measure it in accordance to the FDA. The FDA may encourage them to use a reference material, standard reference material to make sure they're getting the right numbers. FDA may not be handling it themselves.
cues.zh: 花生酱并检测黄曲霉毒素？很多时候，其实是商业实验室按照 FDA 的要求来检测。FDA 可能会鼓励他们使用参考物质，也就是标准参考物质，以确保得到正确的数值。FDA 可能不会自己来处理这件事。

cues.en: There are different challenges to measuring the components of different foods. Fine powder, for example, is easier to characterize than goopy peanut butter.
cues.zh: 测量不同食物的成分会遇到不同挑战。比如细粉末就比黏糊糊的花生酱更容易表征。

cues.en: So it's helpful to have a standard material that closely matches the target
cues.zh: 因此，拥有一种能紧密匹配目标的标准物质会很有帮助，

cues.en: in composition and consistency.
cues.zh: 在组成和一致性上。

cues.en: But it's also impossible for NIST to characterize every different type of food. We're not gonna make a trout and a perch and salmon material, all all these different with the same numbers. We're gonna we're gonna kinda grab an average fish and kinda treat that. So if you're measuring it in other fish, you can usually use it as a surrogate. So you have a standard trout? Correct. Yes.
cues.zh: 但 NIST 也不可能表征每一种不同的食物。我们不会分别做鳟鱼、鲈鱼、三文鱼的标准物质，让所有这些不同的鱼都用同一组数值。我们会大致取一种平均的鱼来处理。所以如果你测的是其他鱼，通常可以把它当作替代物。所以你们有标准鳟鱼？对。是的。

cues.en: Tell me about meat homogenate.
cues.zh: 说说肉匀浆。

cues.en: It is a mixed meat product that has been mixed thoroughly, been ground into a very fine particle, and packed into a very nice tin. Why do you mix, like, chicken and pork? Why not just have, a chicken reference, a pork reference? We we never do this by ourselves. We always work with these industry companies and say, hey, what kind of mixes do you need? And then we request that kind of material to be blended.
cues.zh: 它是一种混合肉制品，经过充分混合、研磨成非常细小的颗粒，并装进一个很漂亮的罐头里。为什么要混合鸡肉和猪肉？为什么不直接做一个鸡肉参考样、一个猪肉参考样？我们自己从不这样做。我们总是和这些行业公司合作，问他们需要什么样的混合物，然后我们要求把那种材料混合起来。

cues.en: For a reference material to be useful, it doesn't have to be the exact material a manufacturer wants to characterize.
cues.zh: 一种参考物质要有用，并不一定非得是制造商想要表征的那种确切材料。

cues.en: It just has to be close enough.
cues.zh: 只要足够接近就行。

cues.en: NIST sells around 30 food items that are spread around their food triangle.
cues.zh: NIST 出售大约 30 种食品，散布在其食品三角图上。

cues.en: At the corners of the triangle are a 100% carbohydrate,
cues.zh: 三角形的三个角分别是 100% 碳水化合物、

cues.en: a 100% fat, and a 100% protein.
cues.zh: 100% 脂肪和 100% 蛋白质。

cues.en: So based on their mix of these three macro ingredients,
cues.zh: 所以，根据这三种宏量成分的配比，

cues.en: all foods fall somewhere on this triangle. And to characterize each one, you would wanna use the closest standard reference material. If you're trying to do your measurements and tell, you know, regulatory authority that I'm making, you know, a food that's a kibble, but I'm measuring it against peanut butter, they're gonna be saying, well, but peanut butter has a wildly different fat content. So what we wanna give them is something, a matrix that looks as much as possible as what they're used to dealing with. They even have a standard diet mix.
cues.zh: 所有食品都会落在该三角形的某个位置。要表征每一种食品，你会想使用最接近的标准参考物质。如果你想进行测量，并告诉监管机构，你知道，我在做一种颗粒干粮，但我拿花生酱来作对照测量，他们就会说，可是花生酱的脂肪含量完全不同。所以我们想给他们的，是一种尽可能接近他们平时处理对象的基质。他们甚至有标准膳食混合物。

cues.en: This is called typical diet.
cues.zh: 这被称为典型饮食。

cues.en: Through surveys, they identified what the average American eats,
cues.zh: 通过调查，他们确定了普通美国人平时吃些什么，

cues.en: and they purchased it all, and they blended it all up, and then they freeze dried it into a nice fine powder. It's a it's a it's like a light gray powder, and this represents all the nutritional components that an average American would consume. So it it represents the sugar content. It represents the proteins that you might have, any vitamins you might have, any fats you might have. It's all in a little jar that we we puree up.
cues.zh: 他们把这些全都买来，全部搅拌混合，再冻干成细腻的粉末。它就像一种浅灰色粉末，代表了普通美国人会摄入的所有营养成分。所以它代表了糖分含量，代表了你可能摄入的蛋白质、各种维生素、各种脂肪。全都在我们打成泥装进的小罐子里。

cues.zh: NIST总共拥有近1,300

cues.zh: 他架起一个摆锤

cues.en: Mhmm. And at the end of a pendulum is a weight. And if you pull that pendulum up to a certain distance,
cues.zh: 嗯。摆锤末端有个重物。如果把摆锤拉到一定距离，

cues.en: you can calculate its potential energy.
cues.zh: 就能算出它的势能。

cues.en: At the bottom of the swing of this pendulum, the arc,
cues.zh: 在摆锤摆动的最低点，也就是弧线底部，

cues.en: is a vise. And in the vise
cues.zh: 是一个台钳。台钳里

cues.en: is held
cues.zh: 夹着

cues.en: a standard piece of metal called a chirpy,
cues.zh: 一块标准金属试样，叫 chirpy，

cues.en: and this has a little v notch in it. So the idea is that the pendulum comes through and breaks this thing, and then it goes up on the other side. And from that, you can then calculate the amount of energy that it took to break this piece of steel. Every company in The United States, and frankly, internationally,
cues.zh: 上面有个小 V 形缺口。原理是摆锤摆过来打断它，然后摆到另一边。由此就能算出打断这块钢所消耗的能量。美国的每一家公司，坦白说，国际上的公司也是，

cues.en: now has to check their materials against our Charpies annually because the kind of steels they're making are used in pipelines or they're used in defense industries, you know, for tanks,
cues.zh: 现在他们每年都得把材料拿来跟我们的 Charpy 试验对照，因为他们生产的那些钢材会用于管道，或者用于国防工业，比如坦克，

cues.en: for things that store nuclear waste. So I I have a joke. I love things that break or burn, these things break, and they have to break, and they can't reuse them, so we sell a lot. How many would you sell in a year? We sell... Of those of all the different kinds, we sell about 8,000.
cues.zh: 还有用来储存核废料的东西。所以我有个玩笑：我就喜欢会断或会烧的东西，这些东西会断，而且必须断，还不能重复使用，所以我们卖得很多。你们一年能卖多少？我们卖……在所有不同种类里，我们大约卖 8,000 件。

cues.en: NIST has been making these standard reference materials for over a century. This is what our very first standard sample number one looks like. It is the real deal,
cues.zh: NIST 制作这些标准参考物质已经有一个多世纪了。这就是我们最早的一号标准样品的样子。它可是货真价实的，

cues.en: and it's gray powder. It's limestone. We are still making
cues.zh: 是灰色粉末。它是石灰岩。我们至今仍在生产

cues.en: limestone number one for a hundred and ten years, and it is still so popular that we sell 40 to 50 units a year of this. Isn't that wild? Very few companies are in existence that are still selling some of their original products, and we do.
cues.zh: 一号石灰岩，已经生产了一百一十年，它仍然很受欢迎，每年能卖出 40 到 50 件。是不是很不可思议？很少有公司还在销售自己最初的产品，而我们就是其中之一。

cues.en: Most of the SRMs we've discussed so far are used for calibration,
cues.zh: 到目前为止，我们讨论的大多数标准参考物质（SRM）都用于校准，

cues.en: but there's another class of SRMs used for validation.
cues.zh: 但还有另一类 SRM 用于验证。

cues.en: This means they're used directly in industry tests to ensure consistency.
cues.zh: 这意味着它们直接用于行业测试，以确保一致性。

cues.en: An example is cigarettes.
cues.zh: 一个例子是香烟。

cues.en: Evidently, smoking in bed was a real issue. You know, people were, like, catching on fire. And so there was a lot of, regulation
cues.zh: 显然，在床上吸烟确实是个大问题。你知道，人们真的会着火。所以当时有很多监管规定

cues.en: as to how,
cues.zh: 关于如何，

cues.en: materials in your mattress or in your sheets or your bed clothes should react to to a combustible source. And we produced some standard cigarettes
cues.zh: 床垫、床单或床上用品中的材料应如何对可燃源作出反应。我们还生产了一些标准香烟

cues.en: that essentially,
cues.zh: 它们基本上，

cues.en: along with the ASTM tests,
cues.zh: 配合 ASTM 测试，

cues.en: would help a manufacturer determine how flammable
cues.zh: 能帮助制造商判断

cues.en: their furniture was or their bedclothes or their their mattress.
cues.zh: 他们的家具、床上用品或床垫有多易燃。

cues.en: And for those tests to be consistent, the fires must be started with a standardized NIST cigarette.
cues.zh: 为了让这些测试保持一致，起火必须用标准化的 NIST 香烟来引燃。

cues.en: Fires started by smoking materials are the leading cause of death by fire in the home in The US.
cues.zh: 在美国，吸烟用品引发的火灾是住宅火灾致死的首要原因。

cues.en: Products like this, but also with the regulations that were in place and just the the educational campaigns that went on have saved many, many lives.
cues.zh: 像这样的产品，再加上当时实施的法规和持续开展的教育宣传活动，已经挽救了许许多多的生命。

cues.en: But they also have standards for things you would never expect, like a standard bullet.
cues.zh: 但他们也为一些你意想不到的东西制定了标准，比如标准子弹。

cues.en: When a bullet is fired through a gun, you know, the rifling in the barrel imparts marks to the bullet. Forensic labs then have to measure these grooves to match the bullet from the crime scene to others fired by the suspected weapon. But how do you know they are accurately measuring the grooves?
cues.zh: 当子弹从枪里射出时，枪管里的膛线会在弹头上留下痕迹。法医实验室得测量这些凹槽，把犯罪现场的子弹和嫌疑武器射出的其他子弹比对。可你怎么知道他们测量得准不准？

cues.en: So this
cues.zh: 所以这个

cues.en: has standard marks on it. They replicated a bullet putting, I believe, essentially nano indentations on it. So very, very fine marks and mapped it on this bullet. They weren't fired to your gun. They were manufactured.
cues.zh: 上面有标准刻痕。他们复制了一颗子弹，我记得是在上面做了纳米级的压痕，非常非常细微的痕迹，然后映射到这颗子弹上。这些不是用你的枪射出来的，是制造出来的。

cues.en: So to validate their equipment, forensic labs can run the standard bullet at the same time as a bullet from a crime scene so they know their measurements are accurate.
cues.zh: 法医实验室可以同时发射标准子弹和犯罪现场子弹，以此来校验设备，确认测量结果准确。

cues.en: The goal of every standard is to quantify something about the world, something important
cues.zh: 每一种标准的目标，都是量化世界上某项重要的东西

cues.en: that's usually pretty hard to measure,
cues.zh: 而这些东西通常很难测量，

cues.en: like house dust.
cues.zh: 比如家里的灰尘。

cues.en: In the early nineties,
cues.zh: 上世纪九十年代初，

cues.en: we worked with maid services
cues.zh: 我们和家政清洁服务合作，

cues.en: and we got vacuum bags. We went to hotels, went to motels, took all the vacuum bags that we got from all of these hotels and houses and everything, mixed it together in a big pot so it's fully mixed. So every little jar has the same number of chemicals, has the same amount of material in it. And then we measured everything in there. And the reason why I find dust is interesting is because dust is from an environmental point of view is a really good way to tell what you and I in our house are being exposed to. Identifying dangerous contaminants is a big part of what these standard reference materials are for, which is why they have several types of lead paint or water from a glacier in Greenland. These are so rare that we have to limit distribution of one unit per customer per three years. Woah. Or dirt from New Jersey and Montana.
cues.zh: 拿到了他们的吸尘器尘袋。我们去了酒店、汽车旅馆，把从这些酒店、住宅等地方收集到的所有尘袋都拿来，倒进一个大桶里充分混合。这样每一小瓶里的化学物质种类和材料量都相同。然后我们测量了里面所有东西。我觉得灰尘有意思，是因为从环境角度看，灰尘能很好地说明你我家里正在接触什么。识别危险污染物正是这些标准参考物质的重要用途之一，这也是为什么他们会有好几种含铅涂料，或来自格陵兰冰川的水。这些东西太稀有了，我们不得不限制发放，每位客户每三年只能领一件。哇。还有新泽西和蒙大拿的泥土。

cues.en: We have a lot of soil samples. They had the permission to go into essentially a contaminated
cues.zh: 我们有很多土壤样本。他们获准进入一片基本上受污染的

cues.en: industrial site in Bozeman, Montana and collect a bunch of rocks in a five gallon pail and bring them back and crunch them up. And so these are certified, again, for things like toxic elements.
cues.zh: 工业场地，就在蒙大拿州博兹曼，采集一堆岩石装进五加仑桶里，带回来粉碎。所以这些样本也经过了认证，比如针对有毒元素的认证。

cues.en: Now the ultimate way to measure what contaminants we're exposed to is by what comes out of us,
cues.zh: 那么，衡量我们暴露于哪些污染物的终极方法，就是看我们排出体外的东西，

cues.en: which is why NIST sells domestic sludge.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么 NIST 会出售生活污泥。

cues.en: This is a record of what has come out of our bodies and down our sewers.
cues.zh: 这是一份记录，记录了我们身体排出、流入下水道的东西。

cues.en: Researchers can examine it for traces of toxins or heavy metals,
cues.zh: 研究人员可以检测其中是否有毒素或重金属的痕迹，

cues.en: contaminants that many of us may be exposed to without knowing.
cues.zh: 这些污染物，我们很多人可能在不知不觉中就会接触到。

cues.en: It's really about environmental monitoring.
cues.zh: 这其实是环境监测。

cues.en: And next year, they're coming out with an actual human poop product. It's been in the news quite a bit is,
cues.zh: 明年，他们会推出真正的人体粪便产品。这东西在新闻里出现过不少次，

cues.en: you know, health is related to your microbiome. Right?
cues.zh: 你知道，健康与你的微生物组有关。对吧？

cues.en: And we're starting to understand that your gut flora and what's in your stomach is hugely important to your health, your mental attitude, just all sorts of things. The fecal matter is an incredibly difficult matrix to measure and extract all the different components out of, and what this material will do is support
cues.zh: 我们开始认识到，肠道菌群、胃里的东西对你的健康、心理状态以及方方面面都极其重要。粪便样本是个极难测量的基质，要从中提取出各种不同成分非常困难，而这种材料能做的是支持

cues.en: measurements of the metabolites, and it will be distributed as a vial of powder, essentially. Do you know how much they got?
cues.zh: 代谢物的测量，最终会以粉末小瓶的形式分发。你知道他们拿到了多少吗？

cues.en: A crapload.
cues.zh: 一大堆。

cues.en: As our knowledge of the world evolves, so too do the standard reference materials stored in this warehouse.
cues.zh: 随着我们对世界的认知不断演变，这座仓库中保存的标准参考物质也在不断更新。

cues.en: NIST is preparing to launch its first living standard reference material next year. The living cells will be hamster ovary cells that can produce monoclonal antibodies.
cues.zh: NIST 正准备明年推出其首个活体标准参考物质。这些活细胞将是能生产单克隆抗体的仓鼠卵巢细胞。

cues.en: Monoclonal antibodies now account for five of the 10 top selling drugs and over $75,000,000,000
cues.zh: 单克隆抗体目前在十大畅销药物中占据五席，并且超过 750 亿美元

cues.en: in annual sales worldwide.
cues.zh: 的全球年销售额。

cues.en: When monkeypox started spreading earlier this year, one issue with diagnosing the disease was that there were no clear laboratory tests to tell if someone was infected.
cues.zh: 今年早些时候猴痘开始传播时，诊断这种疾病的一个难题是：没有明确的实验室检测手段能判断某人是否被感染。

cues.en: NIST was able to create a positive control reference of the monkeypox DNA in just thirty days.
cues.zh: NIST 仅用三十天就制作出了猴痘 DNA 的阳性对照参考品。

cues.en: This warehouse is a very strange place to walk around. So many disparate pieces of our world carefully characterized,
cues.zh: 在这个仓库里走动感觉很奇特。世界上那么多各不相同的东西，被仔细地表征、贴标、打包。

cues.en: labeled, and packaged up. It's a reminder that behind the scenes, invisible to most of us, there are a group of people working tirelessly to ensure that things are what we think they are.
cues.zh: 它提醒我们：在幕后、在大多数人看不见的地方，有一群人正在不知疲倦地工作，确保这些东西确实如我们所想的那样。

cues.en: When we eat peanut butter on toast, we can be sure the peanut butter contains what the label says.
cues.zh: 当我们吃吐司配花生酱时，可以确信花生酱的成分与标签上写的一致。

cues.en: When your blood test comes back with a cholesterol reading, you know it was calibrated with a standard. And when you walk into a steel framed building, you know the steel has the appropriate structural and mechanical properties to hold up that structure.
cues.zh: 当血液检测返回胆固醇读数时，你知道它是用标准品校准过的。当你走进一栋钢结构建筑时，你知道钢材具备支撑该结构所需的适当结构和力学性能。

cues.en: Our world works because unbeknownst to most of us, there is a small army of people diligently checking that what is out there aligns with the standards,
cues.zh: 我们的世界能运转，是因为在大多数人不知情的情况下，有一小群人在勤勉地核查外面的东西是否符合标准，

cues.en: even our poop.
cues.zh: 甚至包括我们的粪便。
